proof_summary: For each prime \(p\), counting pairs divisible by \(p^i\) and applying Legendre’s factorial-valuation formula expresses the quotient’s \(p\)-adic valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1}\delta(\lfloor n/p^i\rfloor)\), where \(\delta(m)=m^2-\sum_{k=1}^m k\lfloor m/k\rfloor\). Each summand is nonnegative, and \(\delta(m)>0\) exactly when \(m\ge3\) (strictness comes from \(k=m-1\)); hence the valuation is positive exactly when \(\lfloor n/p\rfloor\ge3\), equivalently \(p\le\lfloor n/3\rfloor\).
